idiom_name: small struct with unexported fields + validating constructor + `Equal` method
implementation_notes: Go has no operator overloading and cannot customise equality, but structs already have value semantics and the spec gives `==` a field-wise meaning for comparable structs - that is the idiomatic replacement for the classic class with equals/hashCode. The idiom is to keep fields unexported, hand out values through a constructor that validates, and add an `Equal` method whenever equality means more than field identity (as `time.Time.Equal` does); `reflect.DeepEqual` and `google/go-cmp` are for tests, not hot production paths. The method-based form stays the right choice whenever a field would make `==` uncompilable (slices, maps, functions).
pitfalls: A struct containing a slice, map or function is not comparable, so `==` will not compile and equality must be hand-written in an `Equal` method (or checked with `reflect.DeepEqual`, which panics on uncomparable dynamic types).
The zero value is always constructible, so a value bypassing NewMoney equals any other zero value - add an `IsZero`/`Valid` check or make the zero value meaningful.
Values are copied on assignment, so embedding a `sync.Mutex` or other non-copyable state in a value type is a bug that `go vet` copylocks reports.
